summary: An excerpt from Kate Douglas Wiggin's novel Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm (labeled here as Book 11, part 23) describing a bare, under-funded village schoolhouse by the river and how Rebecca is taught there. Rebecca is hard to classify, so teacher Miss Dearborn gives up sorting her into a class; she studies with different groups for different subjects. The passage also introduces Samuel Simpson, nicknamed Seesaw for his indecision, who is drawn to Rebecca's strong character despite her snubs.
one_line: A passage from a fiction book describing a rustic village schoolhouse and Rebecca's unusual classes, plus the introduction of the indecisive pupil Seesaw Simpson.
key_facts: The schoolhouse's villages along the river spent so much money repairing bridges that they were economical with school privileges.
The school had twenty scholars in Rebecca's time.
The room held a teacher's desk and chair on a platform, an uncouth stove blackened at most once a year, a map of the United States, and two black-boards.
A ten-quart tin pail of water and a long-handled dipper sat on a corner shelf.
The higher back seats were envied by the more advanced, longer-legged pupils because they were nearer the windows and farther from the teacher.
Miss Dearborn gave up trying to classify Rebecca after a fortnight.
Rebecca read with Dick Carter and Living Perkins, who were preparing for the academy.
Rebecca recited arithmetic with lisping little Thuthan Thimpthon and geography with Emma Jane Perkins.
Rebecca took grammar after school hours with Miss Dearborn alone.
Rebecca made a poor hand at composition at first because the labor of writing and spelling, plus punctuation and capitals, hindered her expression of ideas.
Rebecca took history with Alice Robinson's class, which was studying the Revolution, and mastered the course up to the Revolution in a week.
Rebecca deliberately held herself back to avoid reciting with the oldest Simpson boy.
Samuel Simpson was called Seesaw because of his difficulty making up his mind.
Seesaw was pale, flaxen haired, blue eyed, round shouldered, and stammered when nervous.
Rebecca snubbed Seesaw to the verge of madness, yet he could never keep his eyes away from her.
